questions.q: What does the reframe I am what I do replace?
a: The belief that you are your inner thoughts
The habit of comparing yourself to others
The fear of being judged at work
The idea that feelings are temporary
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists it first among the Stoic reframes, shifting identity from thought to action.

questions.q: What are the three pillars of Adams's success philosophy?
a: Fake it till you make it, consistency and flexibility
Hard work, natural talent and good luck
Goals, deadlines and external rewards
Focus, discipline and competition
questions.why: Lesson 2 names faking it, consistency over effort, and staying open-minded.

questions.q: What does consistency beats effort mean in practice?
a: Showing up regularly matters more than occasional bursts
Working longer hours is the surest route
Talent is fixed and cannot be trained
One perfect attempt beats many small ones
questions.why: Lesson 2 says a page a day becomes a manuscript, while sporadic effort rarely adds up.

questions.q: Which rule does Adams give for creating your own reframes?
a: A reframe only needs to work, not be true
A reframe must be logically airtight
A reframe should be approved by experts
A reframe must apply to everyone equally
questions.why: Lesson 3 says reframes do not need to be true or logical, only useful to you.

questions.q: What alcohol reframe does the summary offer as an example?
a: Reframing alcohol from a drink into a poison
See alcohol as a reward after a hard day
Treat alcohol as a social obligation
Replace alcohol with sweetened drinks
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the point is not accuracy but whether the reframe helps you drink less.
